title: Arithmetic operators
learningObjectives: Explain arithmetic operators and use JavaScript values and operators predictably.

understand.concept: JavaScript arithmetic operators include addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, remainder, exponentiation, and increment/decrement. The + operator can also concatenate strings, so operand types matter.
understand.whyItMatters: Arithmetic appears in counters, totals, measurements, and calculations. Validate inputs and consider floating-point precision for decimal calculations.
understand.analogy: Arithmetic operators are the calculator keys of the language, but + can also join text.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript coercion, equality, and reference semantics follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The total is 138, the remainder is 2, and exponentiation produces 8.

examples.explanation: The total is 138, the remainder is 2, and exponentiation produces 8.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the values and results described.

practise.guidedTask: Build a bill calculator using addition, multiplication, and remainder. Try adding a number to a string and explain the result.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program using the concept with realistic values. Predict the output before running it and explain any surprising result.
hints: Inspect both value and typeof when needed.
Use explicit conversion and validate its result.
Avoid relying on implicit coercion in security-sensitive logic.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Arithmetic operators</title></head><body>
<script>const subtotal=120;const tax=18;const total=subtotal+tax;const remainder=17%5;console.log(total,remainder,2**3);</script>
</body></html>

questions.explanation: The remainder operator % returns the remainder after division.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to understand a value conversion?
options: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.answer: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.explanation: Explicitly checking conversion results prevents invalid values from silently entering later calculations.
